effects: File exposes synchronous handle state, size and cursor queries, byte reads/writes, flush, EOF adjustment, and timestamps. setPos seeks from file start, movePos from current position, and setEndPos seeks by the supplied signed offset from file end (Windows FILE_END; POSIX SEEK_END); it does not establish a read/write bound or truncate. setSize saves the cursor, sets EOF at the requested size, then restores the cursor.

inputs: Inputs and defaults are declared by the source members listed for `File`; signatures and explicit defaults are preserved in upstream_symbols/defaults.
effects: Creates, copies, renames, moves, and removes files/directories. createFile and deleteFile/deleteFileEx return success booleans; deleteFileThrow and the void mutation functions use their declared exception/error behavior. deleteFileEx retries at most the supplied maxAttempts (default 3); moveDirectory filters entries with the supplied pattern (default "*").
errors: createFile catches all failures and returns false; deleteFile catches all failures and returns false; removeDirectory returns false when the OS removal call fails.

deleteFileThrow throws FileException when unlink/DeleteFile fails. On POSIX its current implementation passes the unlink return value (-1) to translateError rather than errno, so the translated message may not identify the underlying errno.

copyFile throws FileException when opening either endpoint or when a read/write fails. renameFile throws FileException for ordinary rename/MoveFileEx failure; POSIX cross-device rename falls back to copyFile and then calls deleteFile(source) without checking its false result, so it can report success while leaving the source behind.

Windows createDirectory returns false when CreateDirectory fails with ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS and throws FileException for other errors. POSIX ensureDirectory returns raw mkdir status (0 or -1); createDirectory compares that status to EEXIST (17), so an already-existing path yields -1 and is treated as an error, throwing FileException with translateError(-1), rather than returning false. ensureDirectory itself returns the platform directory-creation result without throwing. removeDirectoryForced throws FileException on child-file deletion failure (adding the child path) and then calls removeDirectory without checking its boolean result.

deleteFileEx returns the last deleteFile result after at most maxAttempts attempts, sleeping one second after each failed attempt. moveDirectory ignores ensureDirectory return status and propagates exceptions from recursive moves/renameFile; a failed directory removal can therefore be silent.
behavior.completion: Filesystem mutation calls complete synchronously. No cancellation API is declared.
behavior.cancellation: Not applicable to synchronous declaration/state families; no cancellation API is declared.
resources: Mutations operate on caller-supplied paths and the host filesystem.

inputs: Generated string ordinal/name pairs and optional language XML filename.

USER_CMD_DESCRIPTION = all hubs, "op" = hubs where you're op)
To: PM recipient
Only once: Send only once per user from search frame
In the parameters, you can use %[xxx] variables and date/time specifiers (%Y, %m, ...). The following are available:
%[myNI]: your own nick
%[userNI]: the users nick (user && search context only)
%[userTAG]: user tag (user && search context only)
%[userDE]: user description (user && search context only)
%[userEM]: user email (user && search context only)
%[userSS]: user shared bytes (exact) (user && search context only)
%[userSSshort]: user shared bytes (formatted) (user && search context only)
%[userI4]: user ip (if supported by hub)
%[fileFN]: filename (search context only)
%[line:reason]: opens up a window asking for "reason""
WINAMP_HELP = Default string -> winamp(%[version]) %[state](%[title]) stats(%[percent] of %[length] %[bar])"
WMP_HELP = Default String -> +me %[title] at %[bitrate] <Windows Media Player %[version]>"
effects: The 1,921 linked string enum values form ResourceManager::Strings. Parallel generated arrays provide English default text and normalized lookup names. loadLanguage accepts Language/Strings/String(Name) XML or legacy resources/string(name), resolves relative filenames under AppUtil::PATH_LOCALE, ignores unknown names, and replaces only present names. Omitted entries retain their currently loaded values. Language XML updates rtl from RightToLeft; legacy XML leaves rtl unchanged. Core Exception failures are logged and swallowed, and earlier replacements are not rolled back. UNICODE builds regenerate the wide-string table after successful load.
errors: Malformed/unreadable language files that raise Core Exception are logged as SEV_ERROR under Localizations; loadLanguage returns normally. Other exception classes are not caught by this handler.
behavior.completion: loadLanguage parses and applies values synchronously. getString/getStringW return references into the ResourceManager static arrays.
behavior.cancellation: No cancellation interface exists for synchronous XML loading.
resources: Generated StringDefs.cpp arrays; locale-directory language files; SimpleXML parser; AppUtil locale path; optional Unicode wide-string table.

records.proposed_bridge_requirement: Preserve stable generated string IDs, English defaults, both XML formats, locale path resolution, partial overlays, RTL rules, and logged Core parse failures.

acceptance_scenarios.given: A fresh ResourceManager with generated English defaults and a valid Language XML containing one recognized String plus RightToLeft=true
acceptance_scenarios.when: loadLanguage is called with an absolute path to that file
acceptance_scenarios.then: the recognized string changes, an omitted key remains at its English default, and isRTL returns true.

records.surface_rationale: Localization is a runtime Core capability: generated names/defaults feed string lookups and locale-file overlays used throughout the application.

Separator: Adds a separator to the menu

PM: Sends command as if you sent it by pm

%[userSS]: user shared bytes (exact) (user && search context only)

inputs: No arguments. Compile-time generated version.inc constants; getConfigurationType additionally queries uname on non-Windows.
preconditions: No Core startup or manager instance is required. Accepted distribution generated constants differ from the ignored source checkout and are the binary authority.
effects: getGitCommit returns GIT_COMMIT; getBuildNumber returns numeric GIT_COMMIT_COUNT; getBuildNumberStr stringifies that macro; getVersionTag returns GIT_TAG; getVersionDate returns VERSION_DATE; getAppName/getAppId return static APPNAME_INC/APPID_INC C strings.
getConfigurationType returns x64 on _WIN64, x86 on _WIN32; otherwise uname machine text, or (unknown architecture) on uname failure.

getVersionType returns VERSION_NIGHTLY when the tag has more than four bytes and byte index 4 is 'a', VERSION_BETA for 'b', otherwise VERSION_STABLE. This is the source index test, not general semantic-version parsing.
errors: Functions are noexcept. Allocation failures while constructing returned strings terminate rather than yield a recoverable error. uname failure is represented by the explicit fallback string.
behavior.completion: Synchronous return; no manager, asynchronous completion or network activity.
behavior.cancellation: No cancellation operation.
resources: Generated version.inc is compiled into the binary; no runtime file is read.

ownership_evidence: Returned std::string values are owned copies. Application name/ID are borrowed static C string literals with process lifetime; the Objective-C bridge must return owned NSString values.
threading_evidence: Getter bodies access compiled constants or a local uname buffer without shared manager state. Metadata-only calls do not initialize Core.

errors: These noexcept methods do not return an error object; createToken loops until it finds an unused random token.
